    #Tutorial 1 (Linear Momentum Equation)

    #Question 1

    #Part (a)

    Mass flow rate of water,

    m˙=ρV1​A1​

    m˙=1000(3)⋅π(0.0252)

    m˙=5.8905 kg/s

    Using continuity equation,

    m˙=ρV2​A2​

    V2​=1000π(0.01252)5.8905​

    V2​=12 m/s

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​=P2​+21​ρV2​2+ρgz2​

    P1​+21​(1000)(32)=0+21​(1000)(122)+1000(9.81)(0.75)

    P1​=76183 Pa

    Note that P1​ and P2​ are gauge pressures.

    #Part (b)

    Applying the linear momentum equation,

    ∑F=m˙V2​−m˙V1​

    Forces acting on control volume is equal
    to force due to change in momentum.

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    FH​+P1​A1​−P2​A2​cos45°=m˙V2x​−m˙V1x​

    FH​+76183π(0.0252)=5.8905(12cos45°−3)

    FH​=−117.27 kN (to the left)

    Note that gauge pressure P2​ of the outlet is zero.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    FV​−P2​A2​cos45°=m˙V2y​−m˙V1y​

    FV​=5.8905(12cos45°)

    FV​=49.983 kN (upwards)

    Anchoring force required,

    F=117.272+49.9832​

    F=127.48 kN

    #Question 2

    Force required to tip the block,

    ∑M=0=6(0.0075)−0.05R

    R=0.9 N

    Note that the wall exerts an equal but
    opposite reaction on the control volume.

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    Vnoz​=V1​

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=m˙V2x​−m˙V1x​

    −R=ρAnoz​Vnoz​(0−V1​)

    V1​=1000π(0.0052)0.9​​

    V1​=3.3851 m/s

    By taking a control volume of the fluid nearer to the wall,
    weight of the fluid within it can be considered negligible.

    Minimum flowrate required,

    Q=Anoz​Vnoz​

    Q=π(0.0052)(3.3851)

    Q=265.87×10−6 m3/s

    #Question 3

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    V1​=V2​

    Assuming negligible change in height between V1​ and V2​.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=m˙V2y​−m˙V1y​

    −mg−FA​=ρA1​V1​(V1​cos30°−V1​)

    −9.81m−0.1=1.23π(0.052)(302)(cos30°−1)

    m=0.10854 kg

    #Question 4

    As height of the water column above the nozzle is not negligible, Vnoz​=V1​.

    Force required to suspend plate,

    R=1.5(9.81)=14.715 N

    Linear momentum along z-axis,

    ∑Fz​=m˙V2z​−m˙V1z​

    −R=ρAe​Ve​(0−V1​)

    −14.715=1000π(0.012)(10)(−V1​)

    V1​=4.6839 m/s

    By taking a control volume of the fluid nearer to the wall,
    weight of the fluid within it can be considered negligible.

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    Pe​+21​ρVe​2+ρgze​=P1​+21​ρV1​2+ρgz1​

    21​(1000)(102)=21​(1000)(4.68392)+1000(9.81)h

    h=3.9786 m

    #Tutorial 2 (Angular Momentum Equation)

    #Question 1

    The deflector moves upwards at 10m/s.
    Control volume of interest will then move upwards at 10m/s.
    Taking upwards as the positive y-direction, then VCV​=10 m/s.

    Velocity of air relative to CV,

    Vabs​=Vr​+VCV​

    30=Vr​+10

    Vr​=20 m/s

    Jet of air exits the nozzle with a velocity
    of 20m/s relative to the control volume.

    Using Bernoulli’s equation,

    V1,r​=V2,r​=Vr​

    Assuming negligible change in height between V1​ and V2​.

    Linear momentum along y-axis,

    ∑Fy​=m˙V2y​−m˙V1y​

    −mg−Fanch​=ρA1​V1,r​(V2,r​cos30°−V1,r​)

    −0.1(9.81)−Fanch​=1.23π(0.052)(20)(20cos30°−20)

    Fanch​=−0.46330 N

    Note that the mass flow rate is relative to the control volume.
    Since computed force is negative, the force acts upwards.

    #Question 2

    #Part (a)

    The snowplow is moving to the left at 15m/s.
    Control volume of interest is then moving to the left at 15m/s.
    Taking to the left as the positive x-direction, then VCV​=15 m/s.

    Velocity of snow relative to CV,

    Vabs​=Vr​+VCV​

    0=Vr​+15

    Vr​=−15 m/s

    Since question states effect of gravity is negligible,
    and flow is frictionless, using Bernoulli’s equation,

    V1,r​=V2,r​=Vr​

    Note that the different velocities have the same magnitude, but not direction.

    Relative mass flow rate,

    m˙r​=ρA1​V1,r​

    m˙r​=160(0.2×4)(15)

    m˙r​=1920 kg/s

    Linear momentum along x-axis,

    ∑Fx​=m˙V2x​−m˙V1x​

    Fpush​=ρA1​V1,r​(V2,r​cos45°−V1,r​)

    Fpush​=1920[15cos45°−(−15)]

    Fpush​=49.165 kN (to the left)

    #Part (b)

    Resolving V2,r​ into its components,

    V2x,r​=15cos45°

    V2y,r​=15cos45°

    Since control volume is moving along the x-direction,

    V2x,abs​=15cos45°+15=25.607 m/s

    Control volume has no velocity along the y-direction,

    V2y,abs​=V2y,r​=15cos45°=10.607 m/s

    Magnitude of absolute velocity of the snow,

    V2,abs​=25.6072+10.6072​

    V2,abs​=27.716 m/s

    Direction of velocity vector,

    θ=tan−125.60710.607​

    θ=22.5° (from negative x-axis)

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Mass flow rate into sprinkler,

    m˙=ρAV=ρQ

    m˙=1000(0.001)

    m˙=1 kg/s

    Mass flow rate out of each nozzle,

    m˙noz​=21​m˙=21​(1)=0.5 kg/s

    Velocity of water when it exits nozzle,

    m˙noz​=ρAnoz​Vwater​

    0.5=1000(0.000026)Vwater​

    Vwater​=19.231 m/s

    Note that the velocity is relative to the nozzle.

    Assume resisting torque acts in the anticlockwise direction.

    Angular momentum about z-axis,

    ∑Tz​=m˙(r×V)out​−m˙(r×V)in​

    Tz​=m˙[r(−Vwater​)]

    Tz​=1(0.2)(−19.231)

    Tz​=−3.8462 Nm

    Velocity of water exiting the nozzle is negative
    as it points in the opposite direction of spin.

    Since computed torque is negative, it acts in the clockwise direction.

    #Part (b)

    Tangential velocity of nozzle,

    Vnoz​=rω

    Vnoz​=0.2(500×602π​)

    Vnoz​=10.472 m/s

    Sprinkler is rotating in the anticlockwise direction.

    Tangential velocity of the nozzle is 10.472m/s anticlockwise.
    Water exits nozzle with a velocity of 19.231m/s clockwise, relative to the nozzle.

    Velocity of water relative to CV,

    Vabs​=−Vwater​+Vnoz​

    Vabs​=−19.231+10.472

    Vabs​=−8.759 m/s

    Note that the control volume (dotted lines) is stationary.

    Assume resisting torque acts in the anticlockwise direction.

    Angular momentum about z-axis,

    ∑Tz​=m˙(r×V)out​−m˙(r×V)in​

    Tz​=m˙(rVabs​)

    Tz​=1(0.2)(−8.759)

    Tz​=−1.7518 Nm

    Since computed torque is negative, it acts in the clockwise direction.

    #Part (c)

    Assume angular velocity of sprinkler to be anticlockwise.

    Velocity of water relative to CV,

    Vabs​=−Vwater​+Vnoz​

    Vabs​=−Vwater​+rω

    Vabs​=−19.231+0.2ω

    Note that the control volume (dotted lines) is stationary.

    Angular momentum about z-axis,

    ∑Tz​=m˙(r×V)out​−m˙(r×V)in​

    0=m˙(rVabs​)

    0=1(0.2)(−19.231+0.2ω)

    0=−19.231+0.2ω

    Angular velocity of sprinkler,

    ω=0.219.231​

    ω=96.155 rad/s

    ω=918.21 rev/min

    Since computed value is positive, sprinkler rotates anticlockwise.

    #Tutorial 3 (Energy Equation)

    #Question 1

    Assume fluid flows from the right to the left.
    Mass flow rate of fluid is constant (steady-state).

    Mass flow rate is given by m˙=ρAV.
    Since ρ and A are constants, V is a constant.
    Thus, velocity into and out of the control volume are equal, Vin​=Vout​.

    Using the energy equation in terms of height,

    ρgPin​​+2gVin​2​+zin​+hin​=ρgPout​​+2gVout​2​+zout​+hout​

    ρgPin​​=ρgPout​​+zout​+hloss​

    3=1+1.5+hloss​

    hloss​=0.5 m

    Note that ρgP​ is the height of the fluid column above each point.

    Since computed hloss​ is positive, assumed flow direction is correct.

    #Question 2

    Fluid is discharged steadily, thus m˙=ρAV=const.
    The velocity of the fluid in the pipe is then a constant.

    Pump adds energy to the flow in the pipe and increases flow rate.

    Using the energy equation in terms of height,

    ρgPA​​+2gVA​2​+zA​+hpump​=ρgPB​​+2gVB​2​+zB​+hloss​

    zA​+hpump​=2gV2​+2g1.2V2​

    zA​+hpump​=2g2.2​V2

    Note that VA​≈0 using large tank assumption.

    Volume flow rate is given by,

    Q=AV

    V=AQ​

    V=πr2Q​

    Substituting the above into the equation,

    zA​+20−2000Q2=2g2.2​(πr2Q​)2

    6+20−2000Q2=2(9.81)[π(0.035)2]22.2​Q2

    26−2000Q2=7570.974Q2

    Q=0.052121 m3/s

    #Question 3

    Gauge pressure at outlet,

    P2​=ρgh

    P2​=13600(9.81)(−0.25)

    P2​=−33.354 kPa

    Mass flow rate of water,

    m˙=ρQ

    m˙=1000(4.5)

    m˙=4500 kg/s

    Inlet velocity,

    Vi​=Ai​Q​

    Vi​=π(0.5)24.5​

    Vi​=5.7296 m/s

    Outlet velocity,

    Ve​=Ae​Q​

    Ve​=π(0.6)24.5​

    Ve​=3.9789 m/s

    Using the energy equation in terms of height,

    ρgPi​​+2gVi​2​+zi​+hin​=ρgPe​​+2gVe​2​+ze​+htur​+hloss​

    ρgPi​​+2gVi​2​+zi​=ρgPe​​+2gVe​2​+m˙gW˙tur​​+hloss​

    1000(9.81)415×103​+2(9.81)5.72962​+3=1000(9.81)−33354​+2(9.81)3.97892​+4500(9.81)1.9×106​+hloss​

    hloss​=6.53 m

    Power loss of system,

    W˙loss​=m˙ghloss​

    W˙loss​=4500(9.81)(6.53)

    W˙loss​=288.27 kW

    #Question 4

    Using the continuity equation,

    m˙1​+m˙2​=m˙3​

    ρ1​A1​V1​+ρ2​A2​V2​=ρ3​A3​V3​

    0.5(1.4)+0.2V2​=0.6(2)

    V2​=2.5 m/s

    Note that density is constant throughout.

    Mass flow rates in each section,

    m˙1​=1000(0.5)(1.4)=700 kg/s

    m˙2​=1000(0.2)(2.5)=500 kg/s

    m˙3​=700+500=1200 kg/s

    Note that mass flow rate in each section is different.
    We cannot use the energy equation in terms of height.

    Using the energy equation,

    m˙1​(ρP1​​+21​V1​2)+m˙2​(ρP2​​+21​V2​2)=m˙3​(ρP3​​+21​V3​2)+W˙loss​

    700(100010000​+21.42​)+500(10005000​+22.52​)=1200(1000P3​​+222​)+1500

    P3​=6540.42 Pa

    #Tutorial 4 (Flow Rate Measurement)

    #Question 1

    Using the energy equation,

    ρgP1​​+2gV1​2​+z1​=ρgP2​​+2gV2​2​+z2​

    2gV2​2−V1​2​=ρgP1​−P2​​+(z1​−z2​)

    2gV2​2−V1​2​=ρgρgh1​−ρgh2​​+(−Lsinθ)

    2gV2​2−V1​2​=ρgρgh​+(−Lsinθ)

    V2​2−V1​2=2g(h−Lsinθ)

    Expressing velocity in terms of volume flow rate,

    (A2​Qideal​​)2−(A1​Qideal​​)2=2g(h−Lsinθ)

    A2​2Qideal​2​(1−β4)=2g(h−Lsinθ)

    Qideal​2=A2​2⋅1−β42g(h−Lsinθ)​

    Qideal​=A2​1−β42g(h−Lsinθ)​​

    Ratio of cross-section areas,

    A1​A2​​=4πd2​⋅πD24​

    A1​A2​​=D2d2​

    A1​A2​​=β2

    Accounting for head losses,

    Qactual​=Cv​A2​1−β42g(h−Lsinθ)​​

    Qactual​=4Cv​πd2​1−β42g(h−Lsinθ)​​

    #Question 2

    Velocity upstream of orifice plate,

    Q=A1​V1​=4πD2​V1​

    0.03=4π(0.08)2​V1​

    V1​=5.9683 m/s

    Reynolds number of flow,

    Re=μρVD​=νVD​

    Re=1.12×10−65.9683(0.08)​

    Re=4.2631×105

    From the graph, at β=0.625,

    Co​=0.607

    Flow rate through an orifice meter,

    Q=Co​Qideal​

    Q=Co​A2​ρ(1−β4)2(P1​−P2​)​​

    0.03=0.607π(0.025)21000(1−0.6254)2(P1​−P2​)​​

    P1​−P2​=268.45 kPa

    #Question 3

    Pressure difference of nozzle meter,

    P1​−P2​=ρgh

    P1​−P2​=1000(9.81)(0.0073)

    P1​−P2​=71.613 Pa

    Flow rate through nozzle meter,

    Q=Cn​A2​ρ(1−β4)2(P1​−P2​)​​

    Q=Cn​π(0.025)21.225(1−0.6254)2(71.613)​​

    Q=0.023064Cn​

    Iteration 1

    Assume Cn​=0.96.

    Flow rate through nozzle meter,

    Q=0.96(0.023064)=0.022141 m3/s

    Velocity upstream of nozzle meter,

    V=A1​Q​=π(0.04)20.022141​=4.4048 m/s

    Reynolds number of flow,

    Re=μρVD​=νVD​=1.46×10−54.4048(0.08)​=2.4×104

    From the graph, at β=0.625,

    Cn​=0.965

    Iteration 2

    Assume Cn​=0.965.

    Flow rate through nozzle meter,

    Q=0.965(0.023064)=0.022257 m3/s

    Velocity upstream of nozzle meter,

    V=π(0.04)20.022257​=4.4279 m/s

    Reynolds number of flow,

    Re=1.46×10−54.4279(0.08)​=2.4×104

    From the graph, at β=0.625,

    Cn​=0.965

    After iterating twice, the discharge coefficient Cn​=0.965.

    Q=0.023064(0.965)=0.022257 m3/s

    #Tutorial 5 (Dimensional Analysis)

    #Question 1

    Step 1: List all the variables involved in the problem.

    • Drag force FD​
    • Fluid density ρ
    • Fluid viscosity μ
    • Fluid velocity V
    • Cylinder diameter d
    • Cylinder length l

    Number of variables n=6.

    Step 2: Express each variable in terms of reference dimensions (mass, length, time).

    • FD​=N=s2kg⋅m​=T2ML​=MLT−2
    • ρ=m3kg​=L3M​=ML−3
    • μ=m2N⋅s​=m⋅skg​=LTM​=ML−1T−1
    • V=sm​=TL​=LT−1
    • d=m=L
    • l=m=L

    Number of reference dimensions m=3.

    Number of Π-groups required,

    k=n−m=6−3=3

    Since given repeating variables are ρ, V, and d,
    multiply each of the remaining variables by them.

    Diameter has a more significant impact than length.

    Equations for each Π-group,

    Π1​=(ρa1​⋅Vb1​⋅dc1​)FD​

    Π2​=(ρa2​⋅Vb2​⋅dc2​)μ

    Π3​=(ρa3​⋅Vb3​⋅dc3​)l

    where Π1​=f(Π2​, Π3​)

    Comparing coefficients for Π1​,

    M0L0T0=(ρa1​⋅Vb1​⋅dc1​)FD​

    M0L0T0=(ML−3)a1​(LT−1)b1​(L)c1​(MLT−2)

    M0L0T0=(Ma1​+1)(L−3a1​+b1​+c1​+1)(T−b1​−2)

    ∴ a1​=−1     b1​=−2     c1​=−2

    Comparing coefficients for Π2​,

    M0L0T0=(ρa2​⋅Vb2​⋅dc2​)μ

    M0L0T0=(ML−3)a2​(LT−1)b2​(L)c2​(ML−1T−1)

    M0L0T0=(Ma2​+1)(L−3a2​+b2​+c2​−1)(T−b2​−1)

    ∴ a2​=−1     b2​=−1     c2​=−1

    Comparing coefficients for Π3​,

    M0L0T0=(ρa3​⋅Vb3​⋅dc3​)l

    M0L0T0=(ML−3)a3​(LT−1)b3​(L)c3​(L)

    M0L0T0=(Ma3​)(L−3a3​+b3​+c3​+1)(T−b3​)

    ∴ a3​=0     b3​=0     c3​=−1

    Substituting the constants into Π-groups,

    Π1​=ρ−1⋅V−2⋅d−2⋅FD​=ρV2d2FD​​

    Π2​=ρ−1⋅V−1⋅d−1⋅μ=ρVdμ​

    Π3​=ρ0⋅V0⋅d−1⋅l=dl​

    Relationship between Π-groups,

    Π1​=f(Π2​, Π3​)

    ρV2d2FD​​=f(ρVdμ​, dl​)

    ρV2d2FD​​=f(Re1​, dl​)

    #Question 2

    Step 1: List all the variables involved in the problem.

    • Pressure rise Δp
    • Impeller diameter D
    • Rotational speed ω
    • Fluid density ρ
    • Volume flow rate Q

    Number of variables n=5.

    Step 2: Express each variable in terms of reference dimensions (mass, length, time).

    • Δp=Pa=m2N​=m2kg(m/s2)​=m⋅s2kg​=LT2M​=ML−1T−2
    • D=m=L
    • ω=srad​=s1​=T1​=T−1
    • ρ=m3kg​=L3M​=ML−3
    • Q=sm3​=TL3​=L3T−1

    Number of reference dimensions m=3.

    Number of Π-groups required,

    k=n−m=5−3=2

    Equations for each Π-group,

    Π1​=(Da1​⋅ωb1​⋅ρc1​)Δp

    Π2​=(Da2​⋅ωb2​⋅ρc2​)Q

    where Π1​=f(Π2​)

    Comparing coefficients for Π1​,

    M0L0T0=(Da1​⋅ωb1​⋅ρc1​)Δp

    M0L0T0=(L)a1​(T−1)b1​(ML−3)c1​(ML−1T−2)

    M0L0T0=(Mc1​+1)(La1​−3c1​−1)(T−b1​−2)

    ∴ a1​=−2     b1​=−2     c1​=−1

    Comparing coefficients for Π2​,

    M0L0T0=(Da2​⋅ωb2​⋅ρc2​)Q

    M0L0T0=(L)a2​(T−1)b2​(ML−3)c2​(L3T−1)

    M0L0T0=(Mc2​)(La2​−3c2​+3)(T−b2​−1)

    ∴ a2​=−3     b2​=−1     c2​=0

    Substituting the constants into Π-groups,

    Π1​=D−2⋅ω−2⋅ρ−1⋅Δp=ρω2D2Δp​

    Π2​=D−3⋅ω−1⋅ρ0⋅Q=ωD3Q​

    Relationship between Π-groups,

    ρω2D2Δp​=f(ωD3Q​)

    #Question 3

    #Part (a)

    Step 1: List all the variables involved in the problem.

    • Pressure drop per unit length lΔp​
    • Volume flow rate Q
    • Tube diameter D
    • Dynamic viscosity μ

    Number of variables n=4.

    Step 2: Express each variable in terms of reference dimensions (mass, length, time).

    • lΔp​=m3N​=m3kg(m/s2)​=m2⋅s2kg​=L2T2M​=ML−2T−2
